recipe.notes:
Last-token-pooling embedder (the paper's first-stage retriever) on the stock pooling runner: the bare Qwen3Model architecture hits the ("Model", ("pooling", "embed")) suffix rule (vllm/config/model.py:2327 at the pinned ref, :2288 at the tag), normalises to Qwen3ForCausalLM, and as_embedding_model pools the normalised last hidden state (models/adapters.py:250-255). The checkpoint's own sentence-transformers configs give seq_pooling_type LAST and the normalize activation (transformers_utils/config.py:1023-1055 reads modules.json: the Normalize ENTRY sets use_activation -- the content of 2_Normalize/config.json is never read), so pooler_config stays empty. The checkpoint ships no lm_head with tie_word_embeddings false; the converted pooling class replaces the head with a StageMissingLayer at init, so no hf_overrides are needed (the upstream Qwen3-Embedding-8B has the identical untied, headless shape and is documented-supported).
The template declares the paper's request shapes as data. Documents are encoded as the ONE string "- " + text (experiments/paper/rerankers/reference/octen.py:151-152; octen.yaml:10) -- the prefix is the document shape's fixed head segment, and query_prompt/doc_prompt stay empty so the prefix is not also applied by the client and doubled. Queries run as they are; the paper defines no instruction, and the checkpoint's config_sentence_transformers.json query prompt is NOT part of the recipe. The prefix must ride in the string, never as separately tokenised ids: ids("- " + doc) differ from ids("- ") + ids(doc) (the space merges into the next word; 19 vs 20 ids on a sample document measured when the recipe was written), so the client sends the rendered string and the engine tokenises it whole. The /v1/embeddings route adds the tokenizer's post-processor tokens (renderers/params.py:183), which append the end-of-text anchor (added-token name endoftext, id 151643; NOT the tokenizer_config eos, which is the chat end-of-turn marker 151645) -- declared with add_special_tokens: true, so the budget reserves it, and it is the token the model pools. The shape ends on its content span and pins add_special_tokens: true, declaring the appended token as the shape's anchor: the harness's anchor audit reads the post-processor's tail alone there (the product's TemplateSpec refuses an empty fixed segment, and this content-final declaration is what it offers instead). The checkpoint's ChatML chat template must NOT be served (chat_template: null): vLLM applies no template on /v1/embeddings, and a chat-template counterfactual measured when the recipe was written put the template render at 26 ids vs 7 bare on the sample query under the same special-token regime (8 bare in the default, anchor-appended regime) -- serving it would change every prompt. Do not call the Cohere-shaped /v2/embed with input_type: that route auto-applies the checkpoint's ST prompts ("Instruct: ...\nQuery:" for queries, a single space for documents), both different from the paper (entrypoints/pooling/embed/io_processor.py:77-82,373-392); this recipe pins api openai_embeddings.
Budget: client.max_tokens 8192 counts the model's whole input sequence as the engine sees it -- the "- " prefix, the content and the appended end-of-text anchor together, in the pinned tokenizer's tokens. The content is cut on the client (on_overflow: cut) and the frame is re-attached, so every over-length input keeps the prefix at the head and the anchor at the tail. The paper path makes the same anchor-preserving cut (experiments/paper/rerankers/reference/octen.py:33,64: truncation=True, max_length=8192, right side; HF reserves the post-processor's token -- a truncation check measured 8191 content ids + the appended anchor). The cut BOUNDARY on an over-length input can differ by a token between the two paths (fit cuts at content-token boundaries of the original text and re-renders, the paper cuts the assembled ids), and the render carries the full text over-cap (the truncation happens at encode time in the paper path): the reference never ports the client's cut (docs/how-to/add-a-model.md), so the recipe declares reference.known_deviations: over_cap_cut_differs -- over-cap pairs are reported in the non-gating table and only under-cap pairs gate. Wiring status (post-merge): every request is fitted to the declared budget on the wire by the merged product's embedding client (rcp_ndcg.data.preprocess.fit: content spans cut, frame re-attached), audited in stage 1 against the captured wire; the engine's over-length HTTP 400 (renderers/params.py:485-510) is defense in depth -- loud, never a silent number change. Per-shape query caps (whether query_max_tokens applies): no separate query cap exists in the referent -- the paper path truncates queries and documents alike at 8192 -- so query_max_tokens is not declared and both shapes draw on max_tokens. serve.max_model_len 8192 is defense in depth on the same budget; raising it to serve longer inputs for other clients is a deliberate change (the architecture allows 40960). tokenizer_config.json's model_max_length 131072 exceeds the architecture's max_position_embeddings 40960; the recipe never relies on the tokenizer's limit, and the card's context claims disagree among themselves (README.md:99 says 40,960; its results table says 32,768).
dtype bfloat16 (config.json; the paper loads bf16 explicitly, experiments/paper/rerankers/reference/octen.py:55); vLLM's pooled head normalises in fp32 on both paths. empty_doc: send -- the paper embeds an empty document as the bare "- " prefix; omit_zero would score it 0.0 without sending, which the paper does not do. The reference runs as a subprocess in its own environment (its requirements-reference.txt: torch, transformers>=4.51 for Qwen3; tokenizer-level behaviour verified on transformers 5.17.0); the harness process imports no torch, and the reference module imports none of them at import time (its render mode needs no torch and no transformers; its only third-party imports are numpy, lazily in the embed/score paths, and PyYAML, to read the recipe's declared shapes). Stage 2 compares L2-normalised float32 vectors with the cosine gate; the reference applies the same last-token pooling and the same 1e-12-clamped float32 normalisation as experiments/paper/rerankers/reference/octen.py:22-30,:67. The first GPU wave measured min cosine 0.99362 at the tiny row (ids, pooled token and anchor identical on both sides): the declared gate bound (vec_min_cosine 0.993) carries that evidence, and E2's like-for-like run decides any tightening.

The 0.6B size (the Hub API's default-branch sha re-checked 2026-10-09). Same family as the 8B: config.json architectures [Qwen3Model], model_type qwen3, dtype bfloat16, so the same bare-Qwen3Model -> Qwen3ForCausalLM conversion and the same last-token pooling; the ST configs (config_sentence_transformers.json, modules.json, 1_Pooling, 2_Normalize) carry the identical prompts and pooling chain. Per-size facts: hidden_size 1024 (1_Pooling/config.json word_embedding_dimension 1024; the served vector width, which this family's client block does not declare); max_position_embeddings 32768 (config.json; the architecture's limit -- serve.max_model_len 8192 stays the paper's budget); tie_word_embeddings true (config.json; the 8B's is false) -- vLLM's converted pooling class replaces the lm_head with a StageMissingLayer either way, so the shared hf_overrides {} still needs none; vocab_size 151669; eos_token_id 151643 (the endoftext token, not the 8B's 151645 chat end-of-turn) while tokenizer_config.json's eos stays the im_end marker and the post-processor still appends endoftext 151643, the token the pooler reads. tokenizer.json sha256 def76fb086971c7867b829c23a26261e38d9d74e02139253b38aeb9df8b4b50a (byte-identical to Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B's at 97b0c614..., the base checkpoint the card names); the ChatML chat_template.jinja differs from the 8B's (a newer tool-calling form) and is never served (serve.chat_template null). Weights: 595,776,512 bf16 parameters (model.safetensors 1,191,586,416 B at the pinned revision, Hub tree API); KV at 8192 tokens = 2 x 8 kv heads x 128 head_dim x 28 layers x 2 B = 114,688 B/token, 0.94 GB -- one 80 GB-class GPU with room to spare (the family's resources.gpus 1).
